title: Emission Nebula Sh2-282
caption: The emission nebula Sh2-282, imaged by the Mayall 4-meter Telescope
credit: T.A. Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage) and H. Schweiker (WIYN and NOIRLab/NSF/AURA)

recognition.text: Published in the NSF NOIRLab image archive. No published rating.

story: Red hydrogen gas fills this view of Sh2-282, an HII emission nebula in the constellation Monoceros. Bright blue stars surround the gas, and several pillars are embedded within it.

An HII region is a cloud in which hydrogen atoms have had their electrons stripped away by energetic light. In Sh2-282, the intense light of the bright blue stars energises the hydrogen and makes it glow red.

The pillars are a product of erosion. Radiation and a strong wind of particles streaming from the brilliant blue star at upper left are sculpting them, wearing away thinner gas and leaving denser columns behind. Massive, hot stars shape their birth clouds in this way in many star-forming regions, and pillars like these are among the most recognisable signs of that process at work.

understand.summary: The Mosaic camera on the Mayall 4-meter Telescope used three filters. B is shown in blue, I in orange and hydrogen-alpha in red.

understand.eye: The hydrogen-alpha filter isolates the red glow of hydrogen, and the I filter records near-infrared light the eye cannot see.
